# Reusable nightly automation

Aya exposes one reusable preparation workflow and two composite actions. They
share nightly-update machinery without taking ownership of a caller's pinned
nightly, adapter, validation policy, or promotion credential.

```text
Caller repository                         Aya provider
-----------------                         ------------
Caller workflow ------------------------> nightly-prepare.yml
                                                 |
                                                 v
MODULE.bazel + caller adapter <----------- update-nightly/action.yml
                |                                |
                +--------------------------> scripts/nightly.py
                |
                v
candidate MODULE.bazel [+ MODULE.bazel.lock]
                |
                v
caller's complete CI matrix
                |
                v
caller's protected promotion step -------> promote-nightly/action.yml
                ^                                |
                +------- exact-head CAS <--------+
                |
                v
default-branch commit
```

## Reusable components

- `../workflows/nightly-prepare.yml` resolves the caller's committed pin,
  proposes default-branch candidates, and optionally updates its Bazel lock.
- `update-nightly/action.yml` executes the caller-owned adapter using Aya's
  shared `scripts/nightly.py` helpers from the same provider revision.
- `promote-nightly/action.yml` atomically publishes the validated candidate
  using the caller's own protected credential.

Each caller owns its adapter: Aya uses `scripts/update-rust-nightly.py`, while
bpf-linker keeps its source-selection policy in
`scripts/update-rustc-llvm.py`. The caller also owns its pin, complete CI
matrix, required checks, and protected promotion step.

## Preparation contract

The reusable workflow accepts:

- `updater-script`: required path to an adapter in the caller's checkout.
- `update-lockfile`: whether a candidate also regenerates `MODULE.bazel.lock`.

It returns:

- `rust-nightly`: the committed pin or proposed candidate.
- `module`: the candidate `MODULE.bazel`, encoded as base64, if it changed.
- `module-lock`: the optional candidate lockfile, compressed with gzip and
  encoded as base64 to remain within GitHub Actions output limits.
- `metadata`: optional adapter-owned JSON, such as source commit and version.

Every run resolves the committed pin. Only a default-branch run discovers a
new candidate; pull requests continue using the last committed, validated
nightly. A candidate is promoted only after the caller's complete CI matrix
succeeds. With no candidate, publication is skipped.

## Provider isolation and publication

A reusable workflow runs in its caller's GitHub context, so its checkout
contains the caller repository. The `$/.github/actions/update-nightly`
reference instead resolves the action from Aya at the exact same revision as
the reusable workflow.

The action places that immutable provider's `scripts` directory first in
`PYTHONPATH`, then executes the caller-owned adapter against the caller's
`MODULE.bazel`. Python's `-P` prevents the caller's script directory from
shadowing provider modules; `-B` prevents generated bytecode from appearing
in the checkout.

Preparation receives only a read-scoped workflow token. The caller exposes its
promotion credential only inside its branch-restricted `nightly-promotion`
environment. One GraphQL mutation updates the candidate module and optional
lock together; `expectedHeadOid` prevents publication if the default branch
advanced after validation.

External consumers must pin both reusable provider references to the same
immutable Aya commit. Publish the Aya provider commit before publishing a
consumer that references it. Each caller retains its own nightly pin,
adapter, validation policy, protected environment, and promotion credential.
